goal.statement: Find out who silenced the ferry bell at Greyhollow Ford and get the ferry crossing again before full dark.
goal.success: The bell's clapper is back, the ferry crosses with the party aboard, or the goblins are driven off and the way is clear.
goal.failure: Full dark falls with the ferry still idle, or the party retreats from the ford.

features: A slate-roofed ferry-house on stilts above a brown, fast river.
A bell tower on the ferry-house; its rope hangs cut a yard above the floor.
A flat ferry chained to the near bank; the far bank is lost in reeds.
A causeway of sunk timbers runs downriver into a reed marsh.

portrayal.mood: Uneasy dusk; the river is loud and the birds have gone quiet.
senses: The tang of wet iron from the bell tower.
Woodsmoke from somewhere in the reeds.

secrets: The bell's ring drives off the river-things the goblins fear; they want the clapper for their own camp.
A safe path through the reeds keeps to the old timber posts; off the posts the mud is waist-deep.

beats.summary: The empty ferry-house: a cut bell rope, a pried-open strongbox, small clawed tracks in the mud.

clues.text: Small clawed footprints lead from the ferry-house down to the causeway.
The rope was gnawed through, then cut clean; the bell's clapper is gone, not the bell.
Someone is hiding in the loft above the ferry-house; dust sifts down.

beats.summary: Wenna Marsh, the ferry keeper, hides in the loft. She will tell what she saw and the safe path through the reeds if she is persuaded the party will bring back her grandson and her ferry.

clues.text: She saw four goblins, one with a bell's clapper slung on a cord, head into the reeds.
The safe path keeps to the old timber posts.
Her grandson Pell went after them with a fishing spear; she is frightened for him.

beats.summary: A goblin camp on a mud island in the reeds: a smoky fire, the clapper hung on a pole as a trophy, Pell tied to a post.

portrayal.voice: Clipped river talk; drops the ends of words; swears by 'the old water'.
portrayal.want: Her ferry running and her grandson Pell home before dark.
portrayal.detail: Counts everything in threes under her breath — steps, coins, goblins.
portrayal.appearance: Small, weathered, a boathook she holds like a spear.

knows: Four goblins took the clapper into the reeds.
The safe path keeps to the timber posts.
secrets: She paid the goblins to stay away last winter, and stopped paying this spring.

portrayal.voice: Too loud when scared; tries to sound older than twelve.
portrayal.want: To not be the one who needed rescuing.
portrayal.detail: A fishing spear with a red rag tied below the blade.
portrayal.appearance: Wiry, mud to the knees, rope-burned wrists.

knows: The goblins fear something in the river and ring the clapper against a pot at night.

portrayal.want: To keep the clapper and make the big-feet pay to cross his reeds.
portrayal.detail: Wears the bell's leather clapper-strap as a belt.

knows: The river-things come at full dark.
secrets: He will trade the clapper for safe passage if two goblins fall.
He keeps the clapper because its ring keeps the river-things off his camp.

portrayal.detail: A ferry token from Greyhollow on a cord around her neck.
portrayal.appearance: Tall, scarred knuckles, a soldier's patched cloak.

portrayal.voice: Warm, slow, fond of proverbs he gets slightly wrong.
portrayal.want: To end fights without killing; he believes the goblins can be bargained with.
portrayal.detail: Hums the same three-note hymn whenever he is nervous.
portrayal.appearance: Broad, bald, a river-stone holy symbol on a leather thong.

knows: Goblins will bargain for anything that rings or shines.
secrets: He once failed to save a child at a river crossing.

portrayal.voice: Dry, quick, never more than one sentence at a time.
portrayal.want: To be across the river before dark; she hates water.
portrayal.detail: Flicks a bone die across her knuckles and never rolls it.
portrayal.appearance: Lean, grey-green hood, a bow wrapped in oilcloth.

knows: Goblin camps post a lookout on the highest point.

encounters.name: The reed-camp
encounters.terrain: A mud island thirty feet across, ringed by reeds; the fire gives half cover to anyone behind it; off the island the mud is difficult terrain.
encounters.trigger: The party reaches the island, or the lookout spots them on the causeway.
encounters.morale: When two goblins fall, Snag offers the clapper for safe passage; the rest flee into the reeds if Snag falls.

trackers.name: Full dark falls on the ford
trackers.note: When full, the river-things rise; the scene's failure condition is near.
trackers.advanceWhen: Each beat that spends real time: a long search, a slow approach, a rest.

trackers.name: The reed-camp is alerted
trackers.note: When full, the goblins ambush the party on the causeway instead of waiting at camp.
trackers.advanceWhen: Noise, light, or a failed Stealth check near the reeds.

opening.framing: The party reaches Greyhollow Ford as the light goes amber. The ferry is chained, the ferry-house door hangs open, and the bell that should have rung for them is silent.
